comment: Financial sustainability is appropriately established as a governance mandate, but the principle focuses mainly on continuity of funding. It does not sufficiently address affordability, value for money, cost transparency, technical debt, or the distribution of costs and benefits.

anchor.note: p.54-55 l.Lines 265-271 read as the printed page; section 3.4.2 agrees

public.text: Financial sustainability is appropriately established as a governance mandate, but the principle focuses mainly on continuity of funding. It does not sufficiently address affordability, value for money, cost transparency, technical debt, or the distribution of costs and benefits.
public.suggestedRevision: Expand the mandate to include total cost of ownership, affordability, value realisation, cost allocation, cost transparency, technical-debt management, and equitable distribution of investment and operating costs.
